From: Sophie Li <sophie@ironclad.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-11-28T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Intro + IronClad on‑prem requirements (inventory attached)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for making time today. Per our call, attaching the hardware inventory and a short list of non‑functional requirements we need for the private cluster: predictable 99th pct latency < 120ms for inference, tenant isolation between dev/test/prod, on‑disk encryption with KMS integration, and a snapshot/retention policy for model artifacts.

We expect an initial footprint of 6 rack units (3 racks) with mixed A100s and T4s, and will prioritize low cold‑start latency for short LLM sessions (<=1024 tokens). Can your team propose a node fabric map (node roles + PV strategy) and a short ops charter for handoff to our SREs?

I've attached ironclad‑hw‑inventory.xlsx and a one‑pager of our security checklist.

Thanks,
Sophie Li
Head of Platform, IronClad AI
Sophie Li | IronClad AI

Attachments: ironclad-hw-inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28 KB), ironclad-security-onepager.pdf (pdf, 12 KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-11-29T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + IronClad on‑prem requirements (inventory attached)

Sophie — thanks for the inventory and the checklist. Looping in Monica (DeployOps) and Neha (Security/compliance) to shape the proposal.

High level answer up front: yes — we can satisfy the latency and isolation goals with a small cluster design that uses a split node fabric (inference nodes vs control/ingest/core nodes), local NVMe-backed PVs for model cache, and encrypted blockstore for artifacts with KMS. Proposed next steps:

1) We’ll share a node fabric map that details node roles (inference, batch, modelstore, infra) and CPU/GPU mixes per role.
2) A PV strategy: NVMe ephemeral for KV cache + local model load, ceph/longer‑term blockstore for artifact retention with async replication to S3 gateway for backups.
3) Ops charter: who owns day‑0 (provisioning), day‑1 (rollouts, canaries), and day‑2 (patching, eviction policy).

I attached a quick draft: redwood-nodegrid-proposal-v1.pdf (architecture sketch + initial BOM). Can we target an internal review tomorrow morning PST and a short workshop Friday with your SREs to align network/firewall and KMS details?

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-nodegrid-proposal-v1.pdf (presentation, 48 KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Intro + IronClad on‑prem requirements (inventory attached)

Sophie / Rishi — thanks. A few technical clarifications before the workshop so we can make the sketch actionable:

- Network: Do you require direct cross‑rack L2 adjacency for low latency, or is routed L3 with jumbo frames acceptable? Our preferred pattern is L3 + BGP EVPN for flexibility, but for sub‑120ms p99 we'd like to confirm per‑hop egress.
- Storage: The inventory shows 2x 4TB NVMe per node. Are you comfortable using a small local LVM + cache layer for model hot load and relying on blockstore for persistent model artifacts? We recommend a 3‑tier model: ephemeral NVMe -> local model cache (fs cache) -> encrypted blockstore (Ceph/RBD) -> S3 gateway replication.
- Node sizing: For inference nodes, do you want GPU pinning by tenant or shared multi‑tenant nodepools with cgroup isolation? Shared pools are more efficient but increase blast radius; pinning gives strict isolation.
- Backups & retention: Confirm retention window for model artifacts (30/90/365 days) and compliance holds.

If you can confirm the above, we'll include concrete k8s node selectors, taints/tolerations, PV class definitions, and an ops runbook stub in the workshop deliverable. Friday workshop slot: 2029‑11‑30 10:00–11:30 PST — please confirm.

Monica Patel
DeployOps Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirmations below:

- Network: routed L3 + jumbo frames is fine; we'll provision cross‑rack fiber with dedicated VLANs for control plane and tenant data. BGP EVPN works for our ops team.
- Storage: good with the 3‑tier model. Retention: 90 days for active model artifacts, 365 days for cold archives; we also need an admin action to freeze retention for legal holds.
- Node sizing: we prefer pinning for prod inference tenants and a shared pool for dev/test.
- Workshop: Friday 2029‑11‑30 10:00–11:30 PST works. Arjun and I will join and bring our SRE lead.

Please include a short checklist in your deliverable: network ports required, KMS key policy example, required kernel params for low latency, and an eviction/oom policy draft.

Looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Sophie
Head of Platform, IronClad AI
